thread:
Aisha: FYI support ticket INC-9241 from Acme: their daily usage CSV shows spikes landing on the previous day for a lot of users in CET. Customer says their org timezone is Europe/Berlin.
Devon: @Aisha can you paste the sample CSV they sent? want to check the timestamps.
Aisha: pasted the anonymized rows: `2026-03-28T23:05:12Z, 120` vs `2026-03-29, 8.2` — they expect 23:05 in CET to count on 2026-03-29 not 2026-03-28.
Aisha: attaching screenshot of console daily chart where the same token totals appear under Mar 28 instead of Mar 29 -> https://files.redwood.acme/screenshot-INC9241.png
Devon: thanks. Quick question: was the export requested via the UI Export button or the API export endpoint?
Aisha: UI export, from org admin role. customer says their org default tz is set correctly in org settings (Europe/Berlin).
Devon: ok reproduced locally with an org timezone set to Europe/Berlin. The CSV export code path is using `date_trunc('day', created_at AT TIME ZONE 'UTC')` before applying org offset. so we effectively truncate in UTC then shift -> rows get assigned to previous day when offset is +1/+2.
Samir: that matches a hypothesis I had. The chart (console) uses `created_at AT TIME ZONE org_tz` then `date_trunc('day', ...)` which yields expected results. export path accidentally does `date_trunc('day', created_at)` then `AT TIME ZONE org_tz`. For positive offsets that moves truncated day earlier.
Maya: oh wow. So UI and backend are inconsistent. Customer sees chart + CSV mismatch. This will also affect any downstream billing reconciliation if customers rely on CSVs.
Devon: repro steps I used: 1) create test org with org_tz = 'Europe/Berlin' 2) ingest a usage event at 2026-03-29T00:30:00+02:00 (stored as UTC 2026-03-28T22:30:00Z) 3) open Daily Usage chart (shows 2026-03-29) 4) click Export CSV -> CSV shows date 2026-03-28.
Samir: here's the quick SQL diff to patch (DEV ONLY):
```sql
-- current (buggy)
select date_trunc('day', created_at) as day_utc, sum(tokens) from usage_events where org_id = $1 group by 1;
-- correct behavior
select date_trunc('day', created_at at time zone org_tz) as day_local, sum(tokens) from usage_events where org_id = $1 group by 1;
```
Devon: thanks. Also a gotcha around DST transition days; if org_tz has DST, the UTC shift varies and can flip which calendar day gets counts. Must be careful.
Aisha: customer asked for a hotfix or workaround. any quick mitigation?
Samir: short term: we can re-run the export job server-side transforming timestamps before truncation and provide corrected CSV. I can run a one-off script for INC-9241. Longer term we should fix the export service code and add unit tests for several tz/DST cases.
Maya: prioritize. This looks like P1 for customer-facing billing data. Can we estimate impact and rollout plan?
Devon: impact: all org-level CSV exports since we shipped the export rewrite (2026-02-10) for orgs with non-UTC timezones may be affected. Not every row will move days but many will on +/- offsets.
Samir: plan: 1) create patch for export service (small SQL change) 2) add integration test harness with multiple org_tz (America/Los_Angeles, Europe/Berlin, Asia/Tokyo) 3) run backfill for affected exports older than 30 days on request only 4) default to republish corrected CSVs for customers who open tickets.
Aisha: i'll tell customer we can provide corrected export and that engineering has a patch queued. any ETA?
Samir: I can PR today, request review from @devon, merge and deploy to staging tomorrow, then prod rollout after smoke tests (aiming 48h).
Maya: also file a short postmortem + customer note template. cc @support (for who to notify).
billing-bot: export job INC-9241 corrected_csv_uploaded_by_Samir at 1858770000
Aisha: pinging Acme contact to confirm they'd like the corrected CSV. I'll update the support ticket with the plan.
Devon: I'll add a console metric to track CSV vs chart daily mismatches (quick alert if >0.5% of rows differ) so we catch regressions.
Maya: thanks team. Samir, once patch is merged add the SQL snippet to the PR description and include the integration test matrix.
Samir: will do.
Aisha: closing loop — customer accepted corrected CSV, leaving ticket open until patch is deployed. :white_check_mark:
